nodes.statement: The Ca/Si/Al/O stoichiometry of the glass network controls the defect density of structural voids, which in turn modulates the effective activation energy for ion migration via a percolation threshold.

The thermal expansion coefficient of the glass network modulates the solution space rigidity through a phase transition-like behavior near the glass transition temperature (Tg), where the system exhibits critical slowing down and increased susceptibility to perturbations.

The presence and distribution of structural defects (e.g., non-bridging oxygen atoms, Al substitution sites) in the glass network create localized regions of reduced rigidity, which can be mapped to the bootstrap solution space as regions of high parameter sensitivity and increased variance in model predictions.

The glass network rigidity transitions from floppy to over-constrained at a specific Ca/Si/Al/O stoichiometry, creating a percolation threshold for mechanical stability that correlates with a sharp drop in void correlation length and a peak in activation energy for ion transport.
